question: What is the visibility of a member declared without any access modifier in Java?

options.text: Public: default access means members are visible across the entire application.
Protected: visible to any subclass anywhere and to classes in the same package.
Package-private: accessible only to classes within the exact same package directory.
Private: accessible strictly within the declaring class and invisible elsewhere.

explanation: When no access modifier is specified on a class member, it has package-private (default) access. It can be accessed by any class within the same package, but is completely invisible outside that package.

question: Which access modifiers are permitted on a top-level (non-nested) class declaration in Java?

options.text: Public, protected, package-private, and private are all allowed on top-level classes.
Only protected and public, to permit subclassing across module boundaries.
Only public, because all top-level classes must be accessible across the project.
Only public or package-private (no modifier).

explanation: Top-level classes can only be declared with public or package-private (default) accessibility. Declaring a top-level class as protected or private results in a compilation error.

question: Can a subclass directly access a private field declared in its superclass?

options.text: Yes, private members are inherited and directly visible to all derived subclasses.
Yes, but only if the subclass resides within the same package as the superclass.
Yes, provided the subclass uses the super keyword to qualify the field access.
No, private members are accessible only within the declaring class, never in subclasses.

explanation: Private fields are never directly accessible by name in subclasses, regardless of package location. Subclasses can only manipulate them indirectly via public or protected accessor methods.
